name: Teaching

levels.note: 12th pass + teaching diploma. CTET Paper 1 (Classes 1–5). Age 18–35.
Graduation in relevant subject + B.Ed. CTET Paper 2 (Classes 6–8) or State TET.
Master's degree. UGC-NET or Ph.D for Assistant Professor. Age 21–40.

stages.name: Written Exam
stages.tests: CTET: 150 Qs, 150 min. Child Pedagogy, Subject, Language I & II, EVS/Maths.
stages.note: Qualifying. 60% to pass. Valid for lifetime (from 2021).

stages.name: Interview / Demo
stages.tests: Teaching demo (10–15 min) + personal interview. Subject knowledge + pedagogy.
stages.note: KVS/NVS have interview. State TET recruitments may skip interview (merit-based).

stages.name: Document Verification
stages.tests: Degree, B.Ed, TET certificate, caste, domicile, NOC.
stages.note: B.Ed must be from NCTE-recognised institution. Verify before applying.

stages.name: Medical & Joining
stages.tests: Basic medical fitness. Joining in allotted school/region.
stages.note: KVS/NVS have transferable posts. State boards: home state preference.

syllabus.pattern: 150 questions, 150 marks, 150 minutes: Child Development & Pedagogy 30, Language I 30, Language II 30, Mathematics 30, Environmental Studies 30. No negative marking. Qualifying 60% (90/150).

topics.items: Development and its relation to learning, Piaget, Kohlberg and Vygotsky, socialisation, intelligence, language and thought, gender, individual differences, assessment, inclusive education, learning difficulties
Geometry, shapes and spatial understanding, numbers, addition and subtraction, multiplication and division, measurement, time, money, patterns, data handling, pedagogical issues
Family and friends, food, shelter, water, travel, things we make and do, natural resources, pedagogy of EVS
Comprehension, pedagogy of language development, grammar, teaching-learning materials, remedial teaching

syllabus.books: CTET Paper 1 Guide (Amazon) · Flipkart

syllabus.pattern: 150 questions, 150 marks, 150 minutes: CDP 30, Language I 30, Language II 30, and either Mathematics & Science 60 or Social Science 60. Qualifying 60%.

topics.items: Number system, algebra, geometry, mensuration, data handling; food, materials, the world of the living, moving things, how things work, natural phenomena, pedagogy of science
History (ancient, medieval, modern), geography, social and political life, pedagogy of social science
Same as Paper 1 but at upper-primary level, with more emphasis on inclusive education and assessment

syllabus.pattern: Computer-based written test on subject knowledge, pedagogy, reasoning, general awareness and language, followed by an interview and demo class. Weightage is published in each KVS/NVS notification — read that notice before you prepare.

topics.items: The NCERT syllabus of the subject and the classes you are applying to teach
Teaching methods of that subject, lesson planning, evaluation, child psychology
Reasoning, general awareness, Hindi and English

syllabus.pattern: State TETs follow the CTET structure — Paper 1 for Classes 1–5 and Paper 2 for 6–8 — with state-specific qualifying marks. Several states add a state-specific general studies section.

topics.items: CDP, two languages, mathematics and EVS or science and social science, as in CTET
State GK, state education policy and, in some states, the local language paper

reality: CTET is qualifying only — it doesn't get you a job. You need a recruitment exam (KVS, NVS, state boards) separately.
KVS and NVS are central; state boards are state-specific. Apply to both for more chances.
B.Ed is mandatory for TGT/PGT. Without B.Ed, only PRT (primary) posts are open.
State TET (like UPTET, HTET) is separate from CTET. Some states accept CTET; many require state TET.
Teaching jobs have high competition. KVS PGT attracts 50,000+ applicants for 1000 posts.
Salary: KVS PGT ~₹47,600 (Level 8) + DA + HRA. State varies. Private schools pay less.

faq.q: What is CTET and is it mandatory?
faq.a: Central Teacher Eligibility Test — qualifying exam for teaching Classes 1–8 in central schools (KVS, NVS, Army schools). Mandatory for central recruitment. State schools may require state TET instead.

faq.q: Can a B.Tech graduate become a teacher?
faq.a: Yes. B.Tech + B.Ed makes you eligible for TGT (Maths/Science) in KVS, NVS, and state boards. Some states allow B.Tech without B.Ed for specific subjects.

faq.q: What is the difference between KVS and NVS?
faq.a: KVS = Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (urban, central government employees' children). NVS = Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti (rural, free residential schools). Both central, similar pay, different locations.

faq.q: How many vacancies are there in teaching?
faq.a: KVS recruits 5,000–10,000+ annually. NVS recruits 2,000–3,000. State boards vary widely (UP TGT: 10,000+). Total government teaching vacancies exceed 1 lakh per year.

faq.q: What is the age limit for teaching jobs?
faq.a: KVS: 18–35 years (PRT), 21–35 (TGT/PGT). NVS: similar. State boards: varies (often 21–40). Age relaxations for SC/ST/OBC/PwD.

faq.q: Where do I find official teaching notifications?
faq.a: kvs.gov.in (KVS), navodaya.gov.in (NVS), cbse.gov.in (CTET), and state education boards. SarkariJobs+ links the official notification on every listing.

prepPlan.what: CDP and subject pedagogy carry 30–60 marks and are the most ignored part. Read one pedagogy book cover to cover before subject revision; it also supplies the vocabulary the interview expects.
Revise the NCERT of the subject and class you are targeting, then pick the two languages you score highest in. Language papers are scoring sections, not filler.
Solve 10 years of CTET papers. CTET repeats concepts and often the same pedagogy questions. Track which subject gives you the lowest accuracy and give it double time.
One full 150-question paper a week at exam timing. No negative marking means you should attempt every question — practise that habit in mocks.
KVS, NVS and state interviews include a demo lesson. Practise a 10-minute lesson with a blackboard plan, an activity and a closing question. Record yourself once.
